findings.description: capturing() wraps the caller's `ports` layer with five separate `Layer.effect` blocks (AttributeResolver, RelationshipResolver, DecisionHistory, CustomPredicate, SignatureHistory), and each one independently calls `yield* Layer.build(ports)` (lines 152, 164, 176, 188, 204) to pull out just one service. `Layer.build` called five separate times outside a shared MemoMap does not dedupe against the other four calls, so the underlying `ports` layer (typically a LiveSource's real resolver wiring) is constructed five times instead of once whenever the returned `layer` is provided. If constructing that layer has any side effect (opening a connection, running setup logic, incrementing a counter), that side effect now runs 5x for what the module's own doc comment describes as a single capture pass.
findings.suggestedFix: Build `ports` once (e.g. via `Layer.build(ports)` inside one shared `Effect.gen`/`Layer.effect(Layer.empty, ...)` at the top of `capturing`, or `Layer.memoize`) and derive all five wrapped services from that single built Context, rather than calling `Layer.build(ports)` independently in each of the five `Layer.effect` blocks.

findings.description: The `Filters.text` doc comment says the free-text filter is "matched literally and case-insensitively against subject, action, resource and ids" — but `partsOf`/`searchTextOf` (lines 96-111) also fold `entry.environment` and `entry.evaluationId` into the searched haystack for both `TimelineDecision` and `TimelineOrphan` rows, and `Filters.test.ts` ("matches the evaluation id and the environment", lines 192-200) explicitly asserts that typing an environment name (e.g. "Client") matches rows purely through the text filter. A reader relying on the doc comment's enumerated field list would not expect free text to match on environment at all, even though there is a separate `environment` filter chip that might reasonably be assumed to be the only way to narrow by environment.
findings.suggestedFix: Update the `text` field's doc comment to also name `environment` and `evaluationId` among the matched fields, so the enumerated list matches what `partsOf` actually includes.

findings.description: `rowOf` dispatches on the closed `PortSpan` literal union (`"qadi.attribute" | "qadi.acted" | "qadi.hasCustom" | "qadi.hasSignature" | "qadi.hasRelationship"`) via a chain of `if` statements ending in a `const exhaustive: "qadi.hasRelationship" = name` assignment, rather than `Match.value(name).pipe(Match.when(...), Match.exhaustive)` as AGENTS.md §5a's own example prescribes for "a plain literal union [with] no `_tag`" (its `compare`/`CompareOp` example). Exhaustiveness is still enforced at compile time via the trailing assignment, so this is not a correctness bug, but it is the same kind of manual, non-Match dispatch §5a exists to eliminate, and because it uses `if` rather than a literal `switch (`, it is invisible to `scripts/check-house-style.mjs`'s `SWITCH_BUDGET` gate (which only greps for `\bswitch\s*\(`).
findings.suggestedFix: Convert `rowOf`'s if-chain to a module-scope `Match.value(name).pipe(Match.when("qadi.attribute", ...), ..., Match.exhaustive)` (or `Match.type<PortSpan>()` with `Match.exhaustive`), matching the style already used for `witness`/`refValue` in Remedies.ts and `dispatch` in SimulationSource.ts.

findings.description: 22 of the 26 files in this scope's src/model follow a strict one-source-file-to-one-test-file naming convention (Capture.ts/Capture.test.ts, Gates.ts/Gates.test.ts, etc.). `Selection.ts`, `SimulationEdit.ts`, `SimulationInput.ts` and `Verdict.ts` break that pattern: none has its own `*.test.ts`. Their exports are still exercised, but only indirectly, from other files' suites (`selectionOf`/`Evicted`/`Selected` from `Filters.test.ts`; `composeEdits`/`applyEdits`/`editParts` from `Edits.test.ts`; `subjectOf`/`evaluationOptionsOf` from `Simulation.test.ts`; `verdictOf`/`countsOf` scattered across `Filters.test.ts`, `Pairing.test.ts`, `Replay.test.ts` and `WhatIf.test.ts`). This is defensible for leaf/vocabulary modules but is inconsistent with the rest of the directory and makes it harder to find or extend the tests for those specific functions.
findings.suggestedFix: Either add dedicated `Selection.test.ts`/`SimulationEdit.test.ts`/`SimulationInput.test.ts`/`Verdict.test.ts` files (even if thin, mirroring the pattern used everywhere else), or note in each leaf module's doc comment where its behavior is actually tested so a reader is not left to search for it.
